detailed_summary: The paper presents a general lower bound on the sum of variances for finitely many observables in a C*-algebra. Given Hermitian observables A_1,...,A_d, the variance of each is defined as ⟨A_i^2⟩ - ⟨A_i⟩^2. The main result states that the sum of variances is bounded below by an expression involving the expectations of commutators ⟨i[A_j,A_k]⟩ for j≠k, plus the square of the smallest singular value of an associated localizer. This generalizes uncertainty relations, recovering known bounds in special cases where the commutator term reduces to a root mean square average. The authors also derive a containment relation between Clifford pseudospectra and quadratic pseudospectra for d observables, linking uncertainty principles to pseudospectral theory. The work is set in the abstract framework of C*-algebras, making it applicable to both finite-dimensional quantum systems and infinite-dimensional settings. results_analysis: The main result is a lower bound of the form ∑ Var(A_i) ≥ (1/d) ∑_{j<k} |⟨i[A_j,A_k]⟩|^2 + σ_min(L)^2, where L is the localizer.
